newsitem.title: INDIA: India Leela raises 500 mln rupee debt.
newsitem.headline: India Leela raises 500 mln rupee debt.

text.p: India's Hotel Leela Venture Ltd. is raising 500 million rupees through a private placement of secured, non-convertible debentures, arranger SBI Capital Markets Ltd (SBICAP) told Reuters on Thursday.
Hotel Leela Venture is one of India's leading hotel chains.
The company has an option to retain oversubscription of another 500 million rupees, SBICAP said.

"The funds are being raised to part finance the expansion programme of Hotel Leela Venture involving setting up of two new super deluxe five-star hotels in Bombay and Bangalore and upgradation of the resort at Goa," SBICAP said.
The debentures are secured, non-convertible, redeemable and taxable. The face value of each debenture is 100,000 rupees.
Under Scheme A of the two options offered, investors are entitled to half-yearly interest payment at the rate of 15.25 percent a year, the first payment falling on September 30, 1997.
Under Scheme B, the coupon rate is fixed 1.25 percent above the prime lending rate of India's leading bank State Bank of India. State Bank's current prime rate is 13.5 percent.
The interest rate will be reset every six months on September 30 and March 31 every year benchmarked on the PLR.
The coupon rate is subject to a minimum rate of 14.50 percent per annum and a cap of 16.0 percent per annum.
The Investment Information and Credit Rating Agency (ICRA) has assigned a "LAA+" rating to Leela Venture's debenture programme, indicating high degree of safety with respect to timely repayment.
"We expect to complete the placement in two weeks' time," Arun Bhatnagar, SBICAP's deputy general manager, said.
Hotel Leela Venture would seek listing of the securities on the National Stock Exchange at a later date, he said.
